newsitem.title: USA: LecTec sees profit in fiscal 1997.
newsitem.headline: LecTec sees profit in fiscal 1997.

text.p: Medical company LecTec Corp said Thursday it expects to return to profitability in fiscal year 1997, having implemented a strategic turnaround plan.

On Thursday the company reported a net loss of $15,000 for the fourth quarter ended June 30, versus a loss of $149,000 in the same period last year. For the year, the company reported a loss of $632,000 versus a profit of $154,000.

LecTec attributed the fiscal year loss largely to direct marketing related to its former subsidiary, Natus Corp. In fiscal 1996 it also invested heavily in research and development, including the development of the smoking cessation pill.
LecTec's sales of medical tape and therapeutic products were lower, but the decline was partially offset by increased sales of electrodes and conductive hydrogels, the company said.
